questions.question: A stationary time series has:

options.text: Statistical properties (mean, variance, autocorrelation) that do not depend on time
A constant value over time
No seasonality only if the mean is zero
Values that are all identical

questions.explanation: Weak stationarity requires constant mean and autocovariance that depends only on lag, not on absolute time.

questions.question: In ARIMA(p, d, q), the parameter d represents:

options.text: The number of differencing operations applied to make the series stationary
The number of data points per day
The damping factor of the AR term
The Kalman filter order

questions.explanation: d is the integration order — how many times the series is differenced before fitting the ARMA(p, q) model.

questions.question: What is a disadvantage of recursive multi-step forecasting vs. direct forecasting?

options.text: Recursive forecasting requires retraining for each horizon
Errors compound because predictions are fed back as inputs
It cannot handle multivariate data
It only works with linear models

questions.explanation: Recursive forecasting feeds predicted values into the next step, so forecasting error accumulates across the horizon.

questions.question: What does the forget gate of an LSTM control?

options.text: How much of the previous cell state to retain
Which inputs are discarded entirely before processing
The learning rate for that time step
The gradient clipping threshold

questions.explanation: The forget gate produces values in [0,1] that elementwise multiply the previous cell state, deciding what to retain.

questions.question: When using a sliding window for sequence modeling, the window size should be chosen based on:

options.text: The GPU memory only
The relevant temporal dependency in the data (plus memory constraints)
The number of classes
The optimizer learning rate

questions.explanation: The window must be long enough to capture relevant temporal dependencies (seasonality, lag structure) without exceeding memory budgets.
